content:
sam: heads up — spike of GPU evictions in rack-29 over the last 6h. ~18 evicts, most from node05/node03/node04. pattern: brief PCIe link flap -> Xid 31 -> nvml reset -> pod restart. anyone else seeing this? :warning:

ops-bot: ALERT: rack-29: node05 GPU4 XID 31 detected (2026-03-18T09:22:11Z) :rotating_light:

maria: seeing same. firmware on affected cards 0x1a2b, vendor batch L5K-2025. kernel shows pcie link down then driver reset. pasted short dmesg snippet: 
```
Mar 18 09:22:11 node05 kernel: pcieport 0000:3e:00.0: pcie_link_down
Mar 18 09:22:11 node05 nvidia 0000:84:00.0: GPU 4: Xid (31) - AER UNCORRECTABLE ERROR
Mar 18 09:22:12 node05 nvhost: nvml: reset initiated for GPU 4
Mar 18 09:22:12 node05 kubelet: Pod xyz restarted (killed by driver reset)
```

kevin: can we confirm AER counters and PCIe error stats? run `lspci -vvv -s <bus>` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=serial,pci.bus_id --format=csv -i 4` to map serial -> bus id. also grab `ethtool -S` for the host fabric to rule out NIC resets.

jess: HW note — serial prefixes on those cards match the lot we flagged last quarter. recommend quarantining the five nodes and preparing RMA for the three cards with highest XID counts. I'll ping vendor. @ops-bot please create a ticket. :tools:

ryan: ops plan proposal: 
1) cordon + drain node05,node03,node04 immediately (move batch jobs off)
2) shift batch traffic to rack-12 via routing policy and reduce batch concurrency (batch_size=1) to reduce tail latency and retries
3) enable aggressive prefix caching to reduce token churn for affected services
4) collect nvram dumps, full dmesg, `lspci -vvv`, and power sensor traces for the three hosts

maria: uploaded nvram/dmesg and power logs to /mnt/diag/rack29/1994001234/; added serial list file `rack29_serials_1994001234.csv`.

kevin: quick triage loop to collect ECC counters I ran on node05: 
```
for g in 0 1 2 3 4 5; do echo "GPU $g"; nvidia-smi -i $g --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.device_memory.volatile.total --format=csv; done
```
3 cards show non-zero uncorrected ECC increments aligned with XID timestamps.

jess: vendor rep replied, asked for kernel logs + `lspci -vvv` + power traces. also asked whether ambient PSU rails show transients. ops-bot: ticket #INC-8472 created and vendor contact assigned.

sam: small observation — one host showed a transient GPU thermal jump (70->85C) immediately before the PCIe link drop. could be cabling/wear or cooling transient causing rail sag.

ryan: agreed next steps: 
- schedule 3h maintenance tonight 23:00-02:00 UTC to drain & replace 3 suspect cards
- document timeline & collect: serials, firmware, PCIe AER counters, power/thermal traces, vendor response
- apply temporary routing rule to keep batch away from rack-29 until RMAs complete
I'll open a postmortem doc with the template and owner.

maria: tagging nodes with `gpu:quarantine=rack29` label and adding autoscale override so Dedicated pools don't auto-fill these hosts.

sam: I'll run a rolling GPU stress+validation sweep (low concurrency) across remaining cards after drain to verify stability. will report back in ~2h.

jess: agreed on RMA. add these cards to RMA batch id RMA-2026-03-18-L5K and include serials from `rack29_serials_1994001234.csv`.

ops-bot: NOTE: follow-up actions assigned - cordon/drain nodes (sam), collect traces (kevin/maria), vendor RMA (jess), routing policy change (ryan).

sam: thanks all — will update thread when drain starts. :eyes:
